lines.trans: Carmen! Look at the round blue stamp at the bottom of Ernesto's page!
Approved! Official neighbourhood heritage café and guesthouse: lease protected!
Congratulations, Ernesto! What did the inspector say about Room Nine?
She drank a whole cup of mint tea, ate every crumb of tart, and smiled!
She said restoring a hidden sunroom instead of building walls was brilliant!
And Rocio watched the whole thing proudly from her cushion in the kitchen doorway!
Before walking out to Calle de los Tilos, she asked if the walnut piano really works.
Play it for all of us right now, Carmen: my aunt's finished Courtyard Waltz!
Open the courtyard windows wide, Clara, so Rocio and the whole house can hear.
Windows wide open and afternoon breeze coming in: whenever you are ready, Carmen!
Listen to those first four notes floating out under our lemon tree...
For your aunt, Ernesto, and for Room Nine.

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.text: Vamos a la estación ahora.
examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb with irregular past participle abierto.

examples.text: Abro la ventana por la mañana.
examples.trans: I open the window in the morning.

examples.text: Ayer abrimos la tienda temprano.
examples.trans: Yesterday we opened the shop early.

meanings.note: Ahora mismo means 'right now'.

examples.text: Voy para allá ahora mismo.
examples.trans: I am heading there right now.

examples.text: Ahora tenemos cuatro mesas libres.
examples.trans: Now we have four free tables.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition a + masculine article el; al + infinitive means 'upon doing'.

examples.text: Vamos al mercado por la mañana.
examples.trans: We go to the market in the morning.

examples.text: Al abrir la puerta, sonó el timbre.
examples.trans: Upon opening the door, the bell rang.

meanings.note: Antes de means 'before' a noun or infinitive.

examples.text: Llegué diez minutos antes.
examples.trans: I arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: Antes de salir, cierra la ventana.
examples.trans: Before leaving, close the window.

aprobar.gloss: to approve; to pass (an inspection or exam)

meanings.en: to approve; to pass (an inspection or exam)
meanings.note: Stem-changing o -> ue in stressed present forms (apruebo, aprueba); participle aprobado means 'approved / passed'.

examples.text: El ayuntamiento aprobó la licencia del café histórico.
examples.trans: The city council approved the licence for the historic café.

examples.text: Mi hermana aprobó el examen de música con muy buena nota.
examples.trans: My sister passed the music exam with a very high mark.

meanings.note: Plural azules; azul marino means 'navy blue'.

examples.text: Es una pieza azul.
examples.trans: It is a blue piece.

examples.text: Espere, ¡es azul oscuro, igual que la suya!
examples.trans: Wait, it is dark blue, just like yours!

meanings.note: Bajo llave means 'under lock and key'; as an adjective (bajo/baja), means 'low' or 'ground' (planta baja).

examples.text: Nos sentamos bajo el limonero.
examples.trans: We sit under the lemon tree.

examples.text: Guarda la caja bajo llave.
examples.trans: Keep the box under lock and key.

meanings.note: Local city district with its own shops and squares.

examples.text: El barrio está aquí.
examples.trans: The neighbourhood is here.

examples.text: Vemos los barrios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the neighbourhoods from the door.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: El suelo está limpio y brillante.
examples.trans: The floor is clean and shiny.

examples.text: Tiene unos ojos brillantes.
examples.trans: She has bright eyes.

meanings.note: Denotes a gentle, pleasant wind, especially from the sea or through a shaded courtyard.

examples.text: Una brisa fresca de tarde entraba por la ventana abierta.
examples.trans: A cool afternoon breeze was coming through the open window.

examples.text: Bajo el limonero siempre corre una brisa muy agradable.
examples.trans: Under the lemon tree there is always a very pleasant breeze.

meanings.note: Invariable before masculine or feminine singular nouns (cada día, cada mañana).

examples.text: Abro la cafetería cada mañana.
examples.trans: I open the cafe every morning.

examples.text: Cada habitación tiene su llave.
examples.trans: Each room has its own key.

meanings.note: Plural los cafés (two coffees = dos cafés).

examples.text: El café está aquí.
examples.trans: The coffee is here.

examples.text: Vemos los cafés desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the coffees from the door.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la calle.

examples.text: La calle está aquí.
examples.trans: The street is here.

examples.text: Vemos las calles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the streets from the door.

meanings.note: En casa = at home (without article).

examples.text: La casa está aquí.
examples.trans: The house is here.

examples.text: Vemos las casas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the houses from the door.

meanings.note: Both the kitchen room and the stove/cuisine.

examples.text: La cocina está aquí.
examples.trans: The kitchen is here.

examples.text: Vemos las cocinas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the kitchens from the door.

meanings.note: Drops the written accent in the plural: cojines.

examples.text: Pusimos cojines blancos en los bancos del patio.
examples.trans: We placed white cushions on the courtyard benches.

examples.text: Apoya la espalda contra este cojín blando.
examples.trans: Rest your back against this soft cushion.

meanings.note: Regular -er verb.

examples.text: Comemos juntos a las dos de la tarde.
examples.trans: We have lunch together at two in the afternoon.

examples.text: Comí un trozo de bizcocho de limón.
examples.trans: I ate a piece of lemon sponge cake.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.text: Tomo café con leche caliente.
examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.

examples.text: Habla con calma, por favor.
examples.trans: Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Rental lease or employment agreement.

examples.text: El contrato está aquí.
examples.trans: The contract is here.

examples.text: Vemos los contratos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the contracts from the door.

meanings.note: Unaccented in statements and time clauses (interrogative: cuándo).

examples.text: Avísame cuando llegue el taxi.
examples.trans: Let me know when the taxi arrives.

examples.text: Cuando llueve, huele a tierra mojada.
examples.trans: When it rains, it smells like wet earth.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Tenemos cuatro mesas dentro.
examples.trans: We have four tables inside.

examples.text: La habitación cuatro da al patio.
examples.trans: Room four looks out onto the courtyard.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Querer decir means 'to mean'.

examples.text: ¿Qué dice la carta exactamente?
examples.trans: What does the letter say exactly?

examples.text: Dime la verdad sin miedo.
examples.trans: Tell me the truth without fear.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Soy vecino del barrio.
examples.trans: I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Marks a starting point in space or time.

examples.text: No hablamos desde aquel domingo.
examples.trans: We have not spoken since that Sunday.

examples.text: Abrimos al público desde mañana.
examples.trans: We open to the public starting tomorrow.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.text: El patio tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.

examples.text: Pásame el libro de reservas.
examples.trans: Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

examples.text: Enhorabuena, estoy emocionadísimo.
examples.trans: Congratulations, I'm deeply moved.

examples.text: Yo enhorabuena
examples.trans: I enhorabuena

meanings.note: Sigue entera = it is still in one piece.

examples.text: Es una pieza entera.
examples.trans: It is a whole piece.

examples.text: ¿Y su taza dentro? ¿Sigue entera?
examples.trans: And your cup inside? Is it still in one piece?

entrar.gloss: to come in; to go in; to enter

meanings.en: to come in; to go in; to enter
meanings.note: Pairs with en in Spain (entrar en la posada).

examples.text: Entra mucha luz por el balcón.
examples.trans: Plenty of light comes in through the balcony.

examples.text: Entramos en la tienda para resguardarnos.
examples.trans: We stepped into the shop to shelter.

meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'to' before things (escucha el agua).

examples.text: Escucho los pájaros desde mi cama.
examples.trans: I listen to the birds from my bed.

examples.text: Escuchamos la lluvia sobre las tejas.
examples.trans: We listened to the rain on the tiles.

meanings.note: Forms: ese, esa, esos, esas.

examples.text: Pásame ese cuaderno azul.
examples.trans: Pass me that blue notebook.

examples.text: Esa maleta pertenece a un cliente.
examples.trans: That suitcase belongs to a guest.

flotar.gloss: to float; to drift in the air

meanings.en: to float; to drift in the air
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb used for floating on water or for music and scents drifting through the air.

examples.text: Las hojas amarillas de otoño flotan sobre el agua de la fuente.
examples.trans: The yellow autumn leaves float on the fountain water.

examples.text: Las notas del piano flotaban suaves por todo el patio.
examples.trans: The piano notes drifted softly across the whole courtyard.

meanings.note: Used for lamps, boilers, phones, and keys (never trabajar).

examples.text: La calefacción funciona de maravilla.
examples.trans: The heating works wonderfully.

examples.text: Ayer no funcionaba el timbre viejo.
examples.trans: Yesterday the old buzzer was not working.

meanings.note: In a Spanish house, a long room or balcony closed in with windows; also an art gallery.

examples.text: Desayunamos en la galería por la mañana.
examples.trans: We have breakfast in the sunroom in the morning.

examples.text: La galería de arte abre a las diez.
examples.trans: The art gallery opens at ten.

meanings.note: Plural habitaciones.

examples.text: La habitación está aquí.
examples.trans: The room is here.

examples.text: Vemos las habitaciones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rooms from the door.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.text: Sigue recto hasta el puente.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.

examples.text: Nos quedamos hasta el viernes.
examples.trans: We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Describes heritage buildings and old quarters.

examples.text: Es una pieza histórica.
examples.trans: It is a historic piece.

examples.text: ¡Un arquitecto que trabaja con patios históricos por toda Valencia!
examples.trans: An architect who works with historic courtyard buildings all over Valencia!

meanings.note: Means both a tree leaf and a single sheet of paper.

examples.text: La hoja está aquí.
examples.trans: The leaf is here.

examples.text: Vemos las hojas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the leaves from the door.

meanings.note: Feminine form of inspector.

examples.text: La inspectora revisó los planos y la salida al patio.
examples.trans: The inspector checked the plans and the courtyard exit.

examples.text: Ofrecimos un vaso de agua fresca a la inspectora.
examples.trans: We offered a glass of cool water to the inspector.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.

examples.text: La habitación tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.text: Las ventanas dan al jardín.
examples.trans: The windows face the garden.

examples.text: Desayunamos a las ocho.
examples.trans: We have breakfast at eight.

levantar.gloss: to lift; to raise; to get up (levantarse)

meanings.en: to lift; to raise; to get up (levantarse)
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Levanta esa esquina de la alfombra.
examples.trans: Lift that corner of the rug.

examples.text: Nos levantamos a las seis y media.
examples.trans: We get up at six thirty.

meanings.note: Fruit tree bearing lemons (el limón -> el limonero).

examples.text: El limonero está aquí.
examples.trans: The lemon tree is here.

examples.text: Vemos los limoneros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lemon trees from the door.

lo.gloss: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)

meanings.en: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)
meanings.note: Direct object pronoun before verbs (lo veo), and neuter article in lo que ('what') or lo mejor ('the best').

examples.text: Ya lo veo encima del estante.
examples.trans: I see it now on the shelf.

examples.text: Lo mejor del patio es la calma.
examples.trans: The best part of the courtyard is the calm.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.text: Los vecinos vienen a desayunar.
examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! is Spain's most common everyday farewell.

examples.text: Cruza el puente y luego gira.
examples.trans: Cross the bridge and then turn.

examples.text: ¡Hasta luego, que tengas buen día!
examples.trans: See you later, have a good day!

meanings.note: Té de menta = mint tea.

examples.text: La menta es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The mint is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la menta.
examples.trans: We talk about the mint.

meanings.note: Plural mis (mi llave / mis llaves); unaccented, distinct from pronoun mí.

examples.text: Mi maleta es azul marino.
examples.trans: My suitcase is navy blue.

examples.text: Mis apuntes están en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: My notes are in my pocket.

meanings.note: Singular la miga refers to a single crumb or the soft interior of a loaf (opposite of la corteza); plural las migas means crumbs.

examples.text: La hogaza recién hecha tiene la corteza crujiente y la miga tierna.
examples.trans: The freshly baked loaf has a crisp crust and a tender crumb.

examples.text: Le gustó tanto la tarta de limón que no dejó ni una miga.
examples.trans: She liked the lemon tart so much that she did not leave a single crumb.

mirar.gloss: to look; to look at; to watch

meanings.en: to look; to look at; to watch
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'at' (mira el reloj = look at the clock).

examples.text: Mira qué sol hace esta mañana.
examples.trans: Look how sunny it is this morning.

examples.text: Miramos el mapa antes de salir.
examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

meanings.note: Exterior or structural masonry wall.

examples.text: El muro está aquí.
examples.trans: The thick wall is here.

examples.text: Vemos los muros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the thick walls from the door.

meanings.note: The nut itself is la nuez; de nogal = made of walnut wood.

examples.text: La mesa del comedor es de nogal.
examples.trans: The dining table is made of walnut.

examples.text: Hay un nogal muy viejo en el pueblo.
examples.trans: There is a very old walnut tree in the village.

meanings.note: Feminine all-female plural: nosotras.

examples.text: Nosotros abrimos la posada a las siete.
examples.trans: We open the guesthouse at seven.

examples.text: Siéntese a tomar té con nosotros.
examples.trans: Sit down and have tea with us.

meanings.note: Covers jotted notes, musical notes, and review scores.

examples.text: La nota está aquí.
examples.trans: The note is here.

examples.text: Vemos las notas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the notes from the door.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with the thing possessed (nuestro patio, nuestra posada).

examples.text: Nuestra posada tiene ocho habitaciones.
examples.trans: Our guesthouse has eight rooms.

examples.text: Nuestros vecinos toman café aquí.
examples.trans: Our neighbours have coffee here.

meanings.note: Las nueve = nine o'clock.

examples.text: El tren llega a las nueve en punto.
examples.trans: The train arrives at nine on the dot.

examples.text: Vimos un nueve sobre diez.
examples.trans: We saw a nine out of ten.

meanings.note: Used for hidden architectural features, secret doors, or tucked-away courtyards.

examples.text: Detrás del tabique viejo descubrieron una galería oculta.
examples.trans: Behind the old partition wall they discovered a hidden gallery.

examples.text: La llave estaba en un cajón oculto debajo del mostrador.
examples.trans: The key was in a hidden drawer underneath the counter.

meanings.note: Estar orgulloso de... expresses feeling proud of someone or something.

examples.text: Rocío miraba orgullosa cómo sus aprendices sacaban el pan del horno.
examples.trans: Rocio watched proudly as her apprentices took the bread out of the oven.

examples.text: Estamos muy orgullosos de haber recuperado la sala histórica.
examples.trans: We are very proud to have restored the historic room.

meanings.note: Irregular: oigo, oyes, oye, oímos, oís, oyen; ¡Oiga! / ¡Oye! gets someone's attention.

examples.text: ¿Me oyes bien por teléfono?
examples.trans: Can you hear me clearly on the phone?

examples.text: Acabo de oír pasos en la escalera.
examples.trans: I just heard footsteps on the stairs.

meanings.note: Plural los pares (dos pares de gafas = two pairs of glasses).

examples.text: El par está aquí.
examples.trans: The pair is here.

examples.text: Vemos los pares desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pairs from the door.

meanings.note: Marks destination, recipient (para ti), deadline, and minutes to the hour (cinco para las doce).

examples.text: Este paquete blanco es para mi hermano.
examples.trans: This white parcel is for my brother.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is ten minutes to twelve.

meanings.note: Traditional inner courtyard at the heart of a Spanish building.

examples.text: El patio está aquí.
examples.trans: The courtyard is here.

examples.text: Vemos los patios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the courtyards from the door.

meanings.note: Tocar el piano = to play the piano.

examples.text: Por las tardes alguien toca una melodía suave en el viejo piano del salón.
examples.trans: In the afternoons someone plays a gentle melody on the old parlor piano.

examples.text: Hace veinticinco años daba clases de piano muy cerca de esta calle.
examples.trans: Twenty-five years ago I gave piano lessons very close to this street.

meanings.note: Estar de pie means 'to stand / be standing'; ir a pie means 'to walk'.

examples.text: Después de seis horas de pie agradezco una silla.
examples.trans: After six hours on my feet I welcome a chair.

examples.text: Descansa los pies sobre este taburete bajo de madera.
examples.trans: Rest your feet on this low wooden stool.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.text: Paseamos por el casco antiguo.
examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Charming small inn with rooms around a courtyard.

examples.text: La posada está aquí.
examples.trans: The inn is here.

examples.text: Vemos las posadas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the inns from the door.

meanings.note: Preguntar asks a question; pedir asks for an item or favour.

examples.text: Pregunto en la farmacia por la calle.
examples.trans: I ask at the pharmacy about the street.

examples.text: Una clienta preguntó por el desayuno.
examples.trans: A guest asked about breakfast.

meanings.note: Shortens to primer before masculine singular nouns (el primer día); also used as adverb ('first').

examples.text: Hoy es mi primer día de trabajo.
examples.trans: Today is my first day of work.

examples.text: La primera habitación está libre.
examples.trans: The first room is vacant.

meanings.note: Queda protegido = remains protected.

examples.text: Es una pieza protegida.
examples.trans: It is a protected piece.

examples.text: queda protegido
examples.trans: remains protected

meanings.note: Covers room doors, street doors, and courtyard gates.

examples.text: La puerta está aquí.
examples.trans: The door is here.

examples.text: Vemos las puertas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the doors from the door.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.text: Espero que descanses muy bien.
examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

meanings.note: Sin querer = by accident; querer decir = to mean.

examples.text: ¿Quiere usted café o té caliente?
examples.trans: Would you like coffee or hot tea?

examples.text: Lo abrí sin querer.
examples.trans: I opened it by accident.

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.text: ¿Qué hora es ahora mismo?
examples.trans: What time is it right now?

examples.text: ¡Qué mañana tan luminosa!
examples.trans: What a bright morning!

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: El viejo piano de nogal recupera hoy su sonido.
examples.trans: The old walnut piano gets its sound back today.

examples.text: Tras dos días de descanso recuperarás toda la fuerza.
examples.trans: After two days of rest you will recover all your strength.

meanings.note: Una mesa redonda = a round table.

examples.text: Es una pieza redonda.
examples.trans: It is a round piece.

examples.text: ¿Dónde cuelgo este espejo redondo? ¿A la izquierda de la ventana o a la derecha?
examples.trans: Where do I hang this round mirror? Left of the window or right?

salir.gloss: to go out; to come out; to leave

meanings.en: to go out; to come out; to leave
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg salgo; salir corriendo = run out.

examples.text: El pan acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The bread just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Salgo temprano hacia la estación.
examples.trans: I leave early for the station.

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.text: La puerta se abre despacio.
examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

meanings.note: Postage stamp or official ink stamp.

examples.text: El sello está aquí.
examples.trans: The stamp is here.

examples.text: Vemos los sellos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stamps from the door.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.

examples.text: Esa maleta azul es mía.
examples.trans: That blue suitcase is mine.

meanings.note: Unaccented conjunction, distinct from accented sí ('yes').

examples.text: Avísame si necesitas otra manta.
examples.trans: Let me know if you need another blanket.

examples.text: Mira si queda leche en la nevera.
examples.trans: Check whether any milk is left in the fridge.

sobre.gloss: on; upon; about; out of (nueve sobre diez)

meanings.en: on; upon; about; out of (nueve sobre diez)
meanings.note: Sobre todo = above all / mostly; also a homograph noun el sobre ('envelope').

examples.text: Deja la llave sobre el mostrador.
examples.trans: Leave the key on the counter.

examples.text: Sacó nueve sobre diez en la prueba.
examples.trans: She scored nine out of ten on the test.

meanings.note: Conjugates like reír (sonrío, sonrió); imperative plural: ¡sonreíd!.

examples.text: La panadera siempre sonríe al abrir el horno.
examples.trans: The baker always smiles when opening the oven.

examples.text: Al probar el bizcocho, sonrió enseguida.
examples.trans: Upon tasting the cake, he smiled right away.

su.gloss: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)

meanings.en: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)
meanings.note: Plural sus (su maleta / sus maletas).

examples.text: Aquí tiene su llave, señora.
examples.trans: Here is your key, madam.

examples.text: Sus habitaciones están en la primera planta.
examples.trans: Your rooms are on the first floor.

meanings.note: Por la tarde = in the afternoon; ¡Buenas tardes! = Good afternoon!; llegar tarde = arrive late.

examples.text: ¡Buenas tardes! ¿Tienen una habitación libre?
examples.trans: Good afternoon! Do you have a room free?

examples.text: Perdón por llegar un poco tarde.
examples.trans: Sorry for arriving a little late.

meanings.note: Usual word in Spain for a sweet tart or birthday cake.

examples.text: Hay tarta de chocolate para el postre.
examples.trans: There is chocolate cake for dessert.

examples.text: Mi abuela hace una tarta de manzana riquísima.
examples.trans: My grandmother makes a delicious apple tart.

meanings.note: Una taza de té = a cup of tea.

examples.text: La taza está aquí.
examples.trans: The cup is here.

examples.text: Vemos las tazas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cups from the door.

terminar.gloss: to finish (terminar de + inf = finish doing)

meanings.en: to finish (terminar de + inf = finish doing)
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Termino mi turno a las tres.
examples.trans: I finish my shift at three.

examples.text: Terminamos de pintar antes de comer.
examples.trans: We finished painting before lunch.

tocar.gloss: to touch; to ring (a bell); to play (an instrument)

meanings.en: to touch; to ring (a bell); to play (an instrument)
meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells c -> qu: toqué.

examples.text: Alguien acaba de tocar el timbre.
examples.trans: Someone just rang the bell.

examples.text: De niño tocaba el piano los viernes.
examples.trans: As a boy he played the piano on Fridays.

meanings.note: Todo el día = the whole day; todo el mundo = everyone; sobre todo = mostly.

examples.text: Todo está limpio y en su sitio.
examples.trans: Everything is clean and in its place.

examples.text: Camina todo recto por esta calle.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead down this street.

meanings.note: ¡Toma! = Here you go!; tomar un café = have a coffee.

examples.text: ¿Qué quiere tomar para desayunar?
examples.trans: What would you like to have for breakfast?

examples.text: Toma, aquí tienes la linterna.
examples.trans: Here you go, here is the flashlight.

meanings.note: Accented té ('tea') distinguishes the noun from pronoun te ('you').

examples.text: El té está aquí.
examples.trans: The tea is here.

examples.text: Vemos los tés desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the teas from the door.

meanings.note: Feminine counterpart of el tío ('uncle').

examples.text: La tía de Ernesto tocaba el piano todos los viernes.
examples.trans: Ernesto's aunt played the piano every Friday.

examples.text: Mi tía prepara el mejor bizcocho de limón del barrio.
examples.trans: My aunt bakes the best lemon sponge cake in the neighbourhood.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Plural los valses.

examples.text: El piano suena precioso con este vals antiguo.
examples.trans: The piano sounds lovely with this old waltz.

examples.text: Un vals tiene siempre tres tiempos por compás.
examples.trans: A waltz always has three beats per bar.

meanings.note: Una ventana soleada = a sunny window.

examples.text: La ventana está aquí.
examples.trans: The window is here.

examples.text: Vemos las ventanas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the windows from the door.

meanings.note: Irregular: veo, vi, visto.

examples.text: Desde aquí veo el puente de piedra.
examples.trans: From here I see the stone bridge.

examples.text: ¡Nos vemos luego en el patio!
examples.trans: See you later in the courtyard!

meanings.note: La verdad = honestly / the truth.

examples.text: La verdad está aquí.
examples.trans: The truth is here.

examples.text: Vemos las verdades desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the truths from the door.

vez.gloss: time / occasion (dos veces = twice; en vez de = instead of)

meanings.en: time / occasion (dos veces = twice; en vez de = instead of)
meanings.note: Plural las veces; a veces = sometimes; otra vez = again.

examples.text: La vez está aquí.
examples.trans: The time / occasion is here.

examples.text: Vemos las veces desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the time / occasions from the door.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.

examples.text: Son las siete y cuarto.
examples.trans: It is quarter past seven.
